title: Frisch–Parisi conjecture for prescribed multifractal spectra
statement_utf8:
Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathscr{S}_{d}$ be the set of functions $\sigma:\mathbb{R}\to [0,d]\cup\{-\infty\}$ such that $\sigma$ is concave and continuous, has compact support contained in $(0,+\infty)$, and has maximum $d$. For every $\sigma\in\mathscr{S}_{d}$, there exists a Baire functional space of functions defined on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$.

**Frisch–Parisi conjecture.** In that Baire functional space, any typical element $f$ obeys some multifractal formalism and satisfies

$$
\sigma_f=\sigma.
$$

This conjecture concerns the inverse problem of constructing Baire spaces in which typical functions have a prescribed singularity spectrum and satisfy a multifractal formalism. The source describes it as a formulation considered by Jaffard and notes that Jaffard obtained a partial solution, so the full assertion is not established here.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every d>=1 and admissible sigma; exists a Baire space with residual f realizing sigma.
technical_disposition: Topology, singularity exponent and which multifractal formalism are unspecified; no full-scope construction from this literal record. Compact-support wording also needs source interpretation.

title: Threshold-equality conjecture for commensurate fractional-order chaotic systems
statement_utf8:
Consider a commensurate fractional-order system

$$
{}_0^C\mathrm{D}_t^{\alpha}X=f(X),
$$

with threshold value $\alpha_t$, and let $\bar{\alpha}$ be the maximum stability bound $\alpha_*(E)$ over the equilibrium points associated with the system's chaotic attractor. **Threshold-equality conjecture.** If the system is chaotic with threshold value $\alpha_t$, and $\bar{\alpha}$ corresponds to the equilibrium points associated with the chaotic attractor, then

$$
\alpha_t=\bar{\alpha}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the numerically observed onset threshold for chaos equals the largest equilibrium-point stability bound. In the example discussed, the authors observe $\alpha_t\geq\bar{\alpha}$ and find both values to be $0.940887$; the general equality is presented as a conjecture based on numerical observations.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every commensurate system with a chaotic attractor and a threshold, alpha_t equals the maximal associated equilibrium stability bound.
technical_disposition: Associated equilibrium, threshold and chaos lack exact definitions. Numerical agreement at 0.940887 is not a certificate; equilibrium linearization alone does not control global chaotic onset.

title: Hoshino–Shiraishi formulas for the branching coefficients in ranks two and three
statement_utf8:
Let $s=(s_1,\ldots,s_n)$, let $\theta=\{\theta_{ij}\}_{1\leqslant i<j\leqslant n}$ be nonnegative integers, and define

$$
\phi_i=\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\theta_{ji}+\sum_{j=i+1}^n\theta_{ij}.
$$

The branching coefficients $e_n(s;\theta;q,t)$ are defined by the branching expansion described in the source. **Hoshino–Shiraishi conjectures.** For rank two,

$$
e_2(s_1,s_2;\theta_{12};q,t)=\frac{(t,t/s_1,t/s_2,q^{\theta_{12}+1}/(ts_1s_2);q)_{\theta_{12}}}{(q,q/s_1,q/s_2,q^{\theta_{12}}/(s_1s_2);q)_{\theta_{12}}}\left(\frac qt\right)^{\theta_{12}},
$$

and for rank three, the coefficient is the displayed product formula in the source, with $\theta_{ji}=\theta_{ij}$ for $1\leqslant i<j\leqslant3$. These formulas conjecturally determine the first nontrivial branching coefficients for the folded asymptotically free solutions.
quantifiers_reviewed: All nonnegative theta in ranks two and three and admissible s,q,t; the branching coefficients equal specified products.
technical_disposition: Rank-three product is omitted, coefficient expansion and nonsingular parameter domain absent. Finite rank is not a finite identity without these definitions.

title: The small-dimensional subset conjecture for large spectra
statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $A\subset G$ have density $\alpha$, and let $\eta>0$. Write $\Delta_\eta(A)$ for the $\eta$-large spectrum. For a subset $S$ of an abelian group, its dimension is the size of the smallest set $\Lambda$ such that

$$
S\subset\left\{\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\varepsilon_\lambda\lambda:\varepsilon_\lambda\in\{-1,0,1\}\right\}.
$$

**Small-dimensional spectrum conjecture.** For every $1\geqslant\varepsilon\gg\eta^2$, there exists $\Delta'\subset\Delta_\eta(A)$ such that

$$
|\Delta'|\gg\varepsilon|\Delta_\eta(A)|
$$

and

$$
\dim(\Delta')\lesssim_\alpha \varepsilon\eta^{-2}.
$$

The conjecture is strictly weaker than the spectrum structural conjecture. It is known in the range $1\geqslant\varepsilon\gg\eta$, while the final range $\eta\gg\varepsilon\gg\eta^2$ remains open; the paper notes that the first conjecture implies it.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every finite abelian G,A of density alpha and eta>0; for eta^2 << epsilon <=1 exists a spectrum subset of relative size >>epsilon and dimension O_alpha(epsilon eta^-2).
technical_disposition: Selecting a dissociated subset only gives the usual eta^-2 scale, losing the epsilon improvement. Known epsilon>>eta range does not bridge eta^2<<epsilon<<eta; no small exact certificate route.

title: Uniform symmetry-factor conjecture for pro-isomorphic zeta functions of graded Lie lattices
statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a graded Lie lattice. A grading is a decomposition of the underlying free $\mathbb{Z}$-module compatible with the Lie bracket, and its weight is the corresponding weighted rank; write $\mathrm{wt}(\mathcal{L})$ for the minimum of these weights. Let $\zeta^\wedge_{\mathcal{L},p}(s)$ denote the local pro-isomorphic zeta function. Suppose that there are rational functions $W_1,\dots,W_k\in\mathbb{Q}(X,Y)$ such that, for almost all primes $p$, one of them satisfies $\zeta^\wedge_{\mathcal{L},p}(s)=W_i(p,p^{-s})$. Suppose further that there exist $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that

$$
W_i(X^{-1},Y^{-1})=(-1)^c p^{a-bs}W_i(X,Y)
$$

for every $i$. **Uniform symmetry-factor conjecture.** Then $b=\mathrm{wt}(\mathcal{L})$. The conjecture predicts that the exponent governing the uniform functional-equation symmetry factor is determined by the minimal grading weight. Functional equations are known in several classes of Lie lattices, but the asserted identification of this exponent with the minimal weight is not established in general.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every graded Lie lattice admitting finitely many uniform local rational functions with a common functional equation; its Y-exponent equals minimal grading weight.
technical_disposition: Displayed equation mixes formal X,Y with p,s; grading positivity and pro-isomorphic zeta definitions must be restored. Correcting symbols gives no credit and no uniform exponent mechanism.

title: Finite CRG representation conjecture for edit distance functions
statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a nontrivial hereditary property. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a finite set of colored regular graphs (CRGs) $\mathcal{K}'=\mathcal{K}'(\varepsilon,\mathcal{H})$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ed}_{\mathcal{H}}(p)=\min\left\{g_K(p):K\in\mathcal{K}'\right\}
$$

for all $p\in(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$.

**Finite CRG representation conjecture.** For every nontrivial hereditary property $\mathcal{H}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the edit distance function $\operatorname{ed}_{\mathcal{H}}(p)$ is the pointwise minimum of the finitely many functions $g_K(p)$ associated with the CRGs in some finite set $\mathcal{K}'(\varepsilon,\mathcal{H})$, throughout $p\in(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$.

This conjecture would show that, away from the endpoints $0$ and $1$, edit distance functions of hereditary properties can always be determined by finitely many colored regular graphs. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is known or open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every nontrivial hereditary property and epsilon>0; a finite CRG family realizes ed_H on (epsilon,1-epsilon).
technical_disposition: CRG admissibility and g_K are not defined. Compactness can give finite approximation but not the asserted exact envelope; cannot replace equality with approximation.

title: Alon–Cambie–Kang asymmetric choosability conjecture for bipartite graphs
statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with bipartition $V=A\sqcup B$. Write $\Delta_A$ and $\Delta_B$ for the maximum degrees of vertices in $A$ and $B$, respectively. The graph is $(k_A,k_B)$-choosable if every list assignment giving vertices of $A$ lists of size $k_A$ and vertices of $B$ lists of size $k_B$ admits a proper coloring from the lists.

**Alon–Cambie–Kang conjecture.** Suppose that $\Delta_A,\Delta_B\geq 2$ and that $k_A,k_B$ are positive integers. Then:

1. for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $\Delta_0$ such that $G$ is $(k_A,k_B)$-choosable whenever $k_A\geq\Delta_A^\varepsilon$, $k_B\geq\Delta_B^\varepsilon$, and $\Delta_A,\Delta_B\geq\Delta_0$;
2. there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that $G$ is $(k_A,k_B)$-choosable whenever $k_A\geq C\log\Delta_B$ and $k_B\geq C\log\Delta_A$;
3. there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that $G$ is $(k_A,k_B)$-choosable whenever $\Delta_A=\Delta_B=\Delta$ and

$$
k_B\geq C\left(\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\right)^{1/k_A}\log\Delta.
$$

These are asymmetric generalizations of the Alon–Krivelevich conjecture. The conjecture is stated for general bipartite graphs, while the source discusses corresponding results for complete bipartite graphs; its resolution status is not given.
quantifiers_reviewed: All bipartite graphs and positive list sizes satisfy all three asymptotic/absolute-constant regimes stated in the literal record.
technical_disposition: One complete-bipartite test cannot prove universal list choosability. Standard greedy bounds depend on degrees rather than logarithms; all three clauses require a uniform coloring argument not supplied here.

title: The toughness conjecture for Kneser graphs
statement_utf8:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $n\geq 2k+1$. The vertex set of the Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ is $\binom{[n]}{k}$, with two vertices adjacent exactly when they are disjoint. For a connected graph $G$, define its **toughness** by

$$
t(G)=\min_S\frac{|S|}{c(G\setminus S)},
$$

where the minimum is over vertex cuts $S$ and $c(G\setminus S)$ is the number of remaining components. A maximum independent set is an independent set of largest possible size.

**The toughness conjecture for Kneser graphs.** If $k\geq 5$ and $n\geq 2k+1$, then

$$
t(K(n,k))=\frac{n}{k}-1.
$$

Moreover, if a vertex subset $S$ satisfies

$$
t(K(n,k))=\frac{|S|}{c(K(n,k)\setminus S)},
$$

then $S$ is the complement of a maximum independent set in $K(n,k)$.

The result is known for $k\in\{3,4\}$ for all $n\geq 2k+1$, and for $k\geq 5$ when $n$ is sufficiently large as a function of $k$. The conjecture asks for the remaining range $k\geq 5$ and $n\geq 2k+1$.
quantifiers_reviewed: All k>=5,n>=2k+1; toughness is n/k-1 and every minimizing cut is a complement of a maximum independent set.
technical_disposition: The complement of a largest independent set gives the upper bound only. Need lower bound for every cut plus equality classification in the near-2k range; an individual finite cut cannot establish the general claim.

title: The local antimagic chromatic number conjecture for spiders
statement_utf8:
A **spider** of $d$ legs, denoted by $Sp(y_1,y_2,\ldots,y_d)$, is formed by identifying one end-vertex of each of $d$ paths of lengths $y_1,y_2,\ldots,y_d$; its size is denoted by $q$, and $\chi_{la}(G)$ is the minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels over all local antimagic edge labelings of $G$. For $d\ge 3$, $y_1,y_2,\ldots,y_d\ge 2$, and

$$
d(d+1) \le 2(2q-1),
$$

**The local antimagic spider conjecture.** $\chi_{la}(Sp(y_1,y_2,\ldots,y_d))=d+1$, except for $Sp(2^{[n]},3^{[m]})$ when $(n,m)$ belongs to the listed exceptional set:

$$
(n,m)\in\\{(4,0),(5,0),(6,0),(0,10),(1,8),(1,9),(2,7),(2,8),(3,5),(3,6),(4,4),(4,5),(5,3)\\}.
$$

The conjecture predicts that the lower bound $d+1$ for the local antimagic chromatic number is attained throughout this range, apart from the specified two-leg-length families. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: All d>=3, leg lengths>=2 satisfying d(d+1)<=2(2q-1), excluding thirteen multiplicity pairs; chi_la=d+1.
technical_disposition: The local antimagic bijection and induced sum definition are only named. Even after restoration an all-leg-length labeling with adjacent sums unequal is needed; no bounded certificate covers the unbounded length vector.

title: Bounded complement approximation conjecture for delta invariants
statement_utf8:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a **log Fano pair**, meaning that $(X,\Delta)$ is log Fano, and suppose that $\delta(X,\Delta)\leq 1$. Let $A_{X,\Delta}(E)$ denote the log discrepancy of a prime divisor $E$ over $X$, $S_{X,\Delta}(E)$ its expected vanishing order, and let an **$N$-complement of plt type** $(X,\Delta_i^+)$ be a complement of plt type with complement index $N$. An **lc place** of $(X,\Delta_i^+)$ is a divisor defining a log canonical place of that pair.

**Bounded complement approximation conjecture.** There is a natural number $N$ depending only on $(X,\Delta)$ and a sequence of prime divisors $\{E_i\}$ over $X$ such that

$$
\delta(X,\Delta)=\lim_i\frac{A_{X,\Delta}(E_i)}{S_{X,\Delta}(E_i)},
$$

and, for each $E_i$, one can find an $N$-complement of plt type $(X,\Delta_i^+)$ such that $E_i$ is an lc place of $(X,\Delta_i^+)$.

The preceding theorem establishes the analogous statement without requiring a bounded complement index. This conjecture asks for a single index $N$, depending only on the fixed pair, that works for every divisor in the approximating sequence.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every fixed log Fano pair with delta<=1; exists N and a divisor sequence approximating delta, each an lc place of a plt-type N-complement.
technical_disposition: plt-type complement and expected vanishing orders are not defined. A fixed N is the essential additional requirement; individual unbounded complements do not establish it.

title: Sensitivity conjecture for Cayley graphs of Coxeter groups
statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of a Coxeter group, and let $Q_d$ be the largest subgraph of $G$ isomorphic to a cube. Write $\boldsymbol{\kappa}(G)=d$ for its dimension, and let $\sigma(G)$ denote the least possible maximum degree of an induced subgraph on more than half the vertices of $G$. **Sensitivity conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains a set $K$ of more than half its vertices such that the subgraph induced by $K$ has maximum degree $\lceil\sqrt{d}\rceil$; equivalently, 
$$
\sigma(G)=\lceil\sqrt{\kappa(G)}\rceil.
$$
 This conjecture proposes that the lower bound for sensitivity in Cayley graphs is attained for every Cayley graph of a Coxeter group. The preceding results establish the bound for several Coxeter groups, while the available evidence is based largely on computational results and the general statement remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every Coxeter Cayley graph; a more-than-half induced vertex set has max degree ceil(sqrt(cube dimension)).
technical_disposition: Finite versus infinite Coxeter groups and the generating set must be fixed to interpret half the vertices and largest cube. Cube sensitivity alone gives a lower bound; no global upper construction.

title: Wang and Zhang's refinement for neighbors of the largest letter
statement_utf8:
Let $b_{n,d}(i,j)$ denote the number of ballot permutations of length $n$ with $d$ descents that have $inj$ as a factor, and let $p_{n,d}(i,j)$ denote the number of odd order permutations $\pi$ of length $n$ with $M(\pi)=d$ that have $inj$ as a cyclic factor. Here, a word is a **factor** of another word if it occurs as a contiguous subword, and a word is a **cyclic factor** of a permutation if it is a factor of a word representing one of its cycles.

**Wang and Zhang's refinement.** For all $n$, $d$, and $2\leq j\leq n-1$,

$$
b_{n,d}(1,j)+b_{n,d}(j,1)=2p_{n,d}(1,j).
$$

This refines Spiro's descent-statistic conjecture by tracking the neighbors of the largest letter in the relevant permutations. The source states that this refinement remains open, although the unrefined conjecture is proved in the paper.
quantifiers_reviewed: All n,d and 2<=j<=n-1; the two ballot-neighbor counts sum to twice the odd-order cyclic count.
technical_disposition: M(pi) and ballot convention are not specified. The unrefined bijection need not preserve neighbors of n; a statistic-preserving lift is a real remaining obligation.

title: The minimum-test conjecture for the MSRD non-existence criterion
statement_utf8: Let $(n_1,\ldots,n_t)\in\mathbb{N}_0^t$ with $n_1\geq\cdots\geq n_t$, and let $\mathcal{I}_{(n_1,\ldots,n_t)}=\\{(u_1,\ldots,u_t)\in\mathbb{N}_0^t\mid u_i\leq n_i\text{ for all }i\in[t]\\}$. For $\bm{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_t)$, write $|\bm{u}|=\sum_i u_i$, and let $\omega(\bm{u})$ be the function occurring in the MSRD non-existence criterion. Fix $d<N$, and choose $s\in[t]$ and $\delta\in[n_{s+1}-1]$ so that $\tilde{\bm{u}}=(n_1,\ldots,n_s,\delta,0,\ldots,0)\in\mathcal{I}_{(n_1,\ldots,n_t)}$ and $|\tilde{\bm{u}}|=d+1$; equivalently, $\tilde{\bm{u}}$ is the minimum element, in graded reverse lexicographic order, whose weight is at least $d+1$. Then $\omega(\tilde{\bm{u}})=q^{2m}-1-\frac{q^m-1}{q-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^tq^{\tilde{u}_i}-t\right)$. **Minimum-test conjecture.** If $\omega(\tilde{\bm{u}})\geq0$, then $\omega(\bm{u})\geq0$ for every $\bm{u}\in\mathcal{I}_{(n_1,\ldots,n_t)}$. This would replace the laborious family of tests in the MSRD non-existence criterion by a single test, and is supported by the abundance of examples described in the source; its resolution is not given.
quantifiers_reviewed: All ordered block sizes and allowed q,m,d with d<N; nonnegative omega at greedy weight d+1 implies nonnegative omega at every bounded vector.
technical_disposition: Literal omega is missing. Primary Corollary6.6 restores an alternating Gaussian-binomial sum; minimizing sum(q^u_i) only handles weight d+1, not every larger weight. No sweep or proof attempted.

title: Maximum-entropy extension conjecture for locally consistent marginals
statement_utf8:
Consider a set of locally consistent marginals satisfying the entropy conditions given by Eqs. 
$$
and
$$
. Here, $S(X)$ denotes the entropy of the marginal on region $X$, and $A$, $B$, and $C$ are regions with unions denoted by $AB$, $BC$, and $ABC$. **Maximum-entropy extension conjecture.** The maximum-entropy state consistent with those marginals exists and obeys

$$
S(ABC)=S(AB)+S(BC)-S(B)
$$

for every $A$, $B$, and $C$ such that (i) $A$, $B$, $C$, $AB$, $BC$, and $ABC$ are all disk-like regions and (ii) $A$ and $C$ are not adjacent to each other. This conjecture would provide the reverse direction of the paper’s discussion: suitable local marginal data would determine a global state satisfying the expected entropy-scaling behavior. The source gives no resolution or proof, so the conjecture remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every locally consistent family satisfying two missing entropy conditions; a maximum-entropy extension exists and saturates strong subadditivity for all allowed disk triples.
technical_disposition: The two hypotheses are blank equations. Local consistency alone cannot be substituted for them, and strong subadditivity supplies only one inequality.

title: Halin's end degree conjecture
statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a graph and let an **end** of $G$ be an equivalence class of rays, where two rays are equivalent if there are infinitely many vertex-disjoint paths between them. The **degree** of an end is the maximum cardinality of a collection of pairwise disjoint rays in that equivalence class. Given a set of disjoint equivalent rays in $G$, a **ray graph** is a graph whose vertex set is that set of rays, with an edge $RS$ whenever there are infinitely many disjoint independent $R$--$S$ paths in $G$. A ray graph for an end is a connected ray graph on a degree-witnessing subset of that end.

**Halin's conjecture.** Every graph contains ray graphs for all its ends.

For ends of finite degree, the assertion is straightforward, and it is also known for ends of countably infinite degree, where the ray graph can be chosen as a ray using Halin's grid theorem. The conjecture remains open for ends of uncountable degree.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every graph and every end, including uncountable degree; exists a connected ray graph on a degree-witnessing disjoint family.
technical_disposition: Finite and countable-degree constructions do not settle uncountable degree. A finite certificate cannot demonstrate the needed transfinite coherent choice of independent paths.

title: Uniform projective-basis conjecture for the leading term of minimal codewords
statement_utf8:
Let $t\geq 2$, let $a_\tau\geq 0$ for $\tau\in\mathbb{F}_2^t\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}$, and define

$$
\mathcal{T}_i=\mathbb{F}_2^t\setminus\left\langle\left\{\tau_j:1\leq j<i\right\}\right\rangle\qquad (1\leq i\leq t).
$$

Let $e_1,\dots,e_t$ be the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb{F}_2^t$, let $\mathbf{1}$ be the all-one vector, and set $\mathcal{P}=\{e_1,\dots,e_t,\mathbf{1}\}$. Consider

$$
F(a)=\frac{1}{(t+1)!}\sum_{\tau_1\in\mathcal{T}_1}\sum_{\tau_2\in\mathcal{T}_2}\cdots\sum_{\tau_t\in\mathcal{T}_t}\left(\prod_{i=1}^t a_{\tau_i}\right)a_{\sum_{i=1}^t\tau_i}.
$$

**Uniform projective-basis conjecture.** Subject to

$$
\sum_{\tau\in\mathbb{F}_2^t\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}}a_\tau=k,
$$

$F(a)$ attains its maximum over $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{2^t-1}$ at $a_\tau=k/(t+1)$ for every $\tau\in\mathcal{P}$ and $a_\tau=0$ otherwise. If the variables are additionally required to satisfy $a_\tau\in\mathbb{N}$, the maximum is attained at points with $|a_\tau-a_{\tau'}|\leq 1$ for all $\tau,\tau'\in\mathcal{P}$ and $a_\tau=0$ otherwise. This conjecture would identify the asymptotically dominant configuration for counting minimal codewords via projective bases; the paper presents it as a general optimization problem and does not provide a proof.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every t>=2,k and nonnegative weights summing to k; one projective basis uniformly supported maximizes F; integer balanced-support clause also asserted.
technical_disposition: Exact uniform-all-vectors count beats the claimed optimizer at t=7. However the source already prints an older random-coding lower bound that contradicts its conjectured asymptotic consequence at t=8; stop as source-subsumption risk, no discovery proposal or credit. See projective-route.md.
source_passage: Sections2-4, especially Proposition4.9,Conjecture4.10 and printed random-coding bound; no full dependency audit

title: Howroyd's periodicity conjecture for maximum independent sets
statement_utf8:
Let $G_3(d)$ be the graph on the monomials of degree $d$ in three variables, with two monomials adjacent exactly when their least common multiple has degree $d+1$. Let $\mathbf{a}_3(d)$ denote the number of maximum independent sets of $G_3(d)$. **Howroyd's periodicity conjecture.** The sequence $\{\mathbf{a}_3(d)\}_{d \geq 9}$ is $3$-periodic, with $\mathbf{a}_3(9)=1$, $\mathbf{a}_3(10)=27$, and $\mathbf{a}_3(11)=27$; equivalently, for $d \geq 9$,

$$
\mathbf{a}_3(d)=\begin{cases}1,&d\equiv 0\pmod{3},\\27,&d\not\equiv 0\pmod{3}.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture, attributed to A. Howroyd through OEIS sequence A297557, concerns the eventual periodicity and exact values of the number of maximum independent sets. The paper presents it as motivation for studying these graphs; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
quantifiers_reviewed: All d>=9; maximum-independent-set counts are 1 for d=0 mod3 and 27 otherwise.
technical_disposition: Primary Theorem2.1 already proves residue zero, with its proof inspected in part. Need classify all equality configurations in both other residues; an exact small d count would only repeat computational motivation.
source_passage: Conjecture1.1,Theorem2.1 statement and opening proof,Section4 theorem pointers; not entire proof

title: The merged-star conjecture for second-smallest distance-unbalancedness of trees
statement_utf8: Let $n\geq 5$. For even $n$, let $S_{(n-2)/2}\mathbin{\cdot}S_{(n-2)/2}$ denote the merged star formed from two stars of parameter $(n-2)/2$; for odd $n$, let $S_{(n-3)/2}\mathbin{-}S_{(n-3)/2}$ denote the subdivided merged star formed from two stars of parameter $(n-3)/2$. For a tree $T$, write $\mathrm{uB}(T)$ for its distance-unbalancedness index. **Second-smallest distance-unbalancedness conjecture.** For any $n\geq 5$, depending on whether $n$ is even or odd, respectively, the merged star $S_{(n-2)/2}\mathbin{\cdot}S_{(n-2)/2}$ or the subdivided merged star $S_{(n-3)/2}\mathbin{-}S_{(n-3)/2}$, respectively, is the unique tree of order $n$ having the second smallest possible distance-unbalancedness index among all trees of order $n$. This pattern was observed computationally for orders $5\leq n\leq 15$; the general assertion remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every tree order n>=5; the parity-dependent merged star is the unique second-smallest distance-unbalancedness tree.
technical_disposition: Distance-unbalancedness and star parameter conventions are missing. Without the exact pair-distance statistic there is no faithful Prüfer-code test; finite n<=15 already checked by source is not a full route.

title: Generalized bounded-critical-number conjecture for $I_{s,t}$-free binary matroids
statement_utf8:
Let $1\leq s\leq t$. A **simple binary matroid** is a restriction of a finite binary projective geometry $\operatorname{PG}(n-1,2)$. It is **$I_{s,t}$-free** if, for every rank-$t$ flat of $\operatorname{PG}(n-1,2)$, its intersection with the matroid is not an $s$-element independent flat. The **critical number** is $n-k$, where $k$ is the dimension of a largest subgeometry of $\operatorname{PG}(n-1,2)$ disjoint from the matroid. A matroid is **triangle-free** if it has no triangle restriction.

**Generalized bounded-critical-number conjecture.** For any $1\leq s\leq t$, the simple $I_{s,t}$-free and triangle-free binary matroids have bounded critical number.

This is presented as a more general problem extending the bounded-critical-number conjecture for $I_s$-free matroids. The source does not state a resolution of this general assertion.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every 1<=s<=t; all simple binary matroids that are I_s,t-free and triangle-free have critical number bounded in terms of s,t.
technical_disposition: Critical number concerns avoiding subspaces at all ambient dimensions. Enumeration of a fixed projective space cannot supply the uniform bound; no dimension-reduction invariant identified.

title: The UMR conjecture for the graph family $H_{n,m}$
statement_utf8:
Let an **$m$-cyclic graph** be a connected graph of order $n$ with $n-1+m$ edges. Let $H_{n,0}=K_{1,n-1}$, with a leaf $v$, and for $m>0$ obtain $H_{n,m}$ from $H_{n,m-1}$ by adding an edge between a leaf and $v$. Let UMR mean unimodal maximum reliability among the relevant graphs, and let node cop-win reliability be the probability that the graph remains cop-win after nodes fail independently.

**The UMR conjecture for $H_{n,m}$.** Among all $m$-cyclic graphs, $H_{n,m}$ is UMR with respect to node cop-win reliability for all $n$ sufficiently large.

This extends the proved cases $m=0,1,2$, corresponding respectively to $K_{1,n-1}$, $U_n$, and $B_n$. The conjecture concerns the extremal graph in every higher cyclicity family, but the source gives no resolution beyond the stated computational evidence.
quantifiers_reviewed: For every cyclicity m, all sufficiently large n; H_n,m maximizes node cop-win reliability in the stated UMR sense.
technical_disposition: UMR is expanded inconsistently and reliability comparison domain is unspecified. The iterative leaf construction also has a feasibility range; small m proved cases do not yield all m.

title: The non-negative coefficient conjecture for cylindric partition generating functions
statement_utf8:
Let $c=(c_1,c_2,c_3)$ be a profile, let $P_{n,c}(q)$ be the polynomial defined by

$$
f_{n,c}(q)=\frac{P_{n,c}(q)}{(q^3;q^3)_n},
$$

and let $g_{n,c}=[z^n]G_c(z,q)$. Write $\ell=c_1+c_2+c_3$.

**Non-negative coefficient conjecture.** For any profile $c=(c_1,c_2,c_3)$, the polynomial $P_{n,c}(q)$ has non-negative coefficients. Moreover, if $\ell\not\equiv 0\pmod{3}$, then

$$
g_{n,c}=\frac{Q_{n,c}(q)}{(q;q)_n},
$$

where $Q_{n,c}(q)$ is a polynomial in $q$ with non-negative coefficients and

$$
Q_{n,c}(1)=\left(\frac{(\ell+2)(\ell+1)}{6}-1\right)^n.
$$

This conjecture seeks a positive-coefficient description of generating functions for cylindric partitions beyond the cases established in the paper; the general sum-side structure remains unknown, and the authors state that they do not yet have tools to determine it for arbitrary profiles.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every profile c=(c1,c2,c3) and n; P has nonnegative coefficients; if sum(c) is not 0 mod3 then Q does too with prescribed value at1.
technical_disposition: f_n,c and G_c are not defined; denominator removal is not a positivity proof. Need a full-profile combinatorial model or recurrence preserving positivity.

title: Higher-uniformity unavoidable hypergraph conjecture
statement_utf8:
For $r\ge 2$, let $\mathrm{un}_r(n,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph contained in every $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $e$ edges. For positive quantities, $a\approx b$ means equality up to a multiplicative factor. **Higher-uniformity unavoidable hypergraph conjecture.** For every $r\ge 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, provided $n^{r-1}\ll e\ll n^{r-\varepsilon}$, one has

$$
\mathrm{un}_r(n,e)\approx \min\left\{\frac{e^{\frac{r}{r-1}}}{n^{r-1+\frac{1}{r-1}}},e^{\frac{1}{r}}\right\}.
$$

The formula extends the known $r\le 4$ results to higher uniformities in the final regime. The source presents it as a conjectural generalization, while noting that the assumption $e\ll n^{r-\varepsilon}$ is imposed because the complementary range can be handled by a separate generalization.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every r>=2,epsilon>0 and n^(r-1)<<e<<n^(r-epsilon); unavoidable size has the asserted two-term minimum order.
technical_disposition: A lower construction must occur inside every e-edge r-graph. Known r<=4 instances give no higher-uniformity embedding theorem; no finite witness can prove the full asymptotic two-sided statement.

title: Generic Kerr bounded-phase-space diffusion conjecture
statement_utf8:
Define the bounded-motion region

$$
\mathcal B(C):=\left\{0<E^2<1,\ |L_z|<C,\ 0<Q<C\mid -R(r^*)>0,\ -R(r_*)<0\right\}\cap H^{-1}\left(-\frac12\right),
$$

where $R$ is the Kerr radial potential, $r^*$ is the local maximum of $-R$, and $r_*$ is the local minimum of $-R$ to its right. **Generic Kerr bounded-phase-space diffusion conjecture.** For a generic stationary perturbation of the Kerr metric, for every $\delta>0$ and $C>0$, an orbit exists that is $\delta$-dense on $\mathcal B(C)$, provided $\varepsilon$ is small. The same assertion holds for a generic perturbation that is $1$-periodic in $\tau$.

This is the Kerr analogue of the conjectured dense-orbit statement for bounded Schwarzschild motions. It is motivated by applying Arnold diffusion to the Liouville-Arnold region, but the source gives no resolution evidence.
quantifiers_reviewed: For generic stationary or time-periodic Kerr perturbations, all delta,C>0 and small epsilon; exists a delta-dense bounded-region orbit.
technical_disposition: Generic topology, energy shell and perturbation quantifier dependencies are unspecified. Arnold diffusion similarity does not prove access to every part of the region.

title: Trautmann's conjecture on maximum-size cyclic subspace codes
statement_utf8: Let $q$ be a prime power, let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers with $k\leq n/2$, and let $\mathcal{G}_q(n,k)$ denote the set of $k$-dimensional $\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_q$-subspaces of $\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_{q^n}$. A cyclic subspace code is a subset of $\mathcal{G}_q(n,k)$ closed under multiplication by every element of $\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_{q^n}^*$; its minimum distance is measured by $d(U,V)=\dim_{\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_q}(U)+\dim_{\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_q}(V)-2\dim_{\operatorname{\mathbb{F}}_q}(U\cap V)$. **Trautmann's conjecture.** For every positive integers $n,k$ such that $k\leq n/2$, there exists a cyclic code of size $\frac{q^n-1}{q-1}$ in $\mathcal{G}_q(n,k)$ and minimum distance $2k-2$. This concerns cyclic subspace codes attaining the maximum possible orbit size; the parser supplies no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved, so its status remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every prime power q and 1<=k<=n/2; exists a cyclic k-subspace code of orbit size (q^n-1)/(q-1) and minimum distance 2k-2.
technical_disposition: k=1 makes the literal size impossible for n>=2 because all lines already form an orbit of that size but distance is2 rather than asserted0. This is a domain/exact-distance correction, excluded from credit. For intended k>=2 a full-orbit Sidon-space construction and prior check are needed.

title: The expander spanning-subgraph conjecture with large girth
statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a finite graph with vertex set $V(G)$. For a subset $S\subset V(G)$ with $0<|S|\leq |V(G)|/2$, let $\partial_G S$ denote its edge boundary, and define the Cheeger constant by

$$
h(G):=\inf_{\substack{S\subset V(G),\\0<|S|\leq |V(G)|/2}}\frac{|\partial_G S|}{|S|}.
$$

For a graph $H$, write $\operatorname{diam}(H)$ for its diameter and $\operatorname{girth}(H)$ for its girth. **The expander spanning-subgraph conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ and natural number $D$ there exist $\kappa,K>0$ such that if $G$ is a finite graph with maximum degree at most $D$ and $h(G)>\varepsilon$, then $G$ admits a spanning subgraph $H$ with

$$
h(H)>\kappa\quad\textrm{and}\quad\operatorname{diam}(H)<K\operatorname{girth}(H).
$$

The conjecture asserts that bounded-degree graphs with uniformly positive expansion contain spanning subgraphs that retain positive expansion while having girth proportional to their diameter. The paper proves it for regular expander graphs with sufficiently large expansion, using the Lovász Local Lemma; the general bounded-degree case remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every epsilon>0,D; exist positive kappa,K so every finite degree<=D epsilon-expander has a spanning kappa-expander with diameter<K*girth.
technical_disposition: Deleting short cycles can destroy the last expansion edges. A local lemma route for regular high-expansion graphs does not bridge arbitrary bounded-degree expanders; no invariant retaining all cuts identified.

title: Incidence-density conjecture for complete bipartite subgraphs
statement_utf8:
Fix $\epsilon>0$. In $\mathbb R^d$, let $\mathcal P$ be a collection of $n$ points and $\mathcal H$ a collection of $m$ hyperplanes. Let $\operatorname{I}(\mathcal P,\mathcal H)$ denote their number of incidences, and let $\operatorname{rs}(\mathcal P,\mathcal H)$ denote the maximum product of the sizes of a point subset and a hyperplane subset forming a complete bipartite incidence subgraph.

**Incidence-density conjecture.** For every fixed $\epsilon>0$, if

$$
\operatorname{I}(\mathcal P,\mathcal H) \geq \epsilon mn,
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{rs}(\mathcal P,\mathcal H) \geq mn\cdot 2^{-O_\epsilon(\sqrt d)}.
$$

The conjecture is the strongest bound discussed under the sole hypothesis of constant incidence density, and would give a bound close to the best currently known communication-complexity estimate, but it is too weak to imply the log-rank conjecture. The source notes constructions with complete-bipartite density $2^{-\Theta(\sqrt d)}$, showing that the exponent has the best possible order.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every fixed epsilon>0; all point-hyperplane systems with incidence density>=epsilon contain a complete rectangle of density 2^-O_epsilon(sqrt(d)).
technical_disposition: Density gives a large-degree vertex but not a rectangle with both sides large. An ambient-dimensional compression lemma is needed; dimension-fixed examples do not settle the exponent.

title: Monotonicity and threshold conjecture for optimal spreading under fixed-size access
statement_utf8: In the fixed-size access model, let $N$ be the number of nodes, $m$ the redundancy level, $r$ the number of accessed nodes, and $b1$ the spreading parameter, with minimal spreading corresponding to $b1=1$ and maximal spreading corresponding to the largest feasible value of $b1$. **Fixed-size spreading conjecture.** Given $N$ and $m$, the optimal $b1$ increases as $r$ increases. Moreover, for every $N$ and $m$, there exists a $b3\frac{b6}{(1,N)}$ such that minimal spreading is optimal for all $rb7b3$, and there exists a $b6b5b6b5(1,N)$ such that maximal spreading is optimal for all $rb7b6$. These assertions would characterize low-access and high-access regimes for the service-rate-maximizing allocation, complementing the paper's sufficient conditions for minimal-spreading optimality and non-optimality.
quantifiers_reviewed: All N,m; optimal spreading is monotone in accessed count r and has minimal/maximal threshold regimes.
technical_disposition: Threshold symbols are corrupted and neither objective nor feasible set is given. No meaningful exact optimization can be run without restoring the service model.

title: The extremal digraph conjecture for directed paths
statement_utf8:
Let $P_{k+1}$ be the directed path on $k+1$ vertices, let ${\rm ex}(n,\overrightarrow{P_{k+1}})$ denote the maximum number of arcs in an $\overrightarrow{P_{k+1}}$-free digraph of order $n$, and let ${\rm EX}(n,\overrightarrow{P_{k+1}})$ be the family of extremal digraphs. For $n\ge 3k$, let $\overrightarrow{T_{n,k}}$ be the corresponding $k$-partite transitive tournament construction, let $a(D)$ denote the number of arcs of a digraph $D$, and let $\overrightarrow{\mathcal{T}_{n,k}}$ be the family of its extremal constructions.

**The extremal digraph conjecture for directed paths.** For every $k,n\in \mathbb{N}^*$ with $n\ge 3k$,

$$
{\rm ex}(n,\overrightarrow{P_{k+1}})=a(\overrightarrow{T_{n,k}}),
$$

and

$$
{\rm EX}(n,\overrightarrow{P_{k+1}})=\overrightarrow{\mathcal{T}_{n,k}}.
$$

The result is known for directed paths of lengths corresponding to the established cases $k=2$ and $k=3$, but the general assertion for all $k$ and $n\ge 3k$ remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every k>=1,n>=3k; extremal directed-path-free size and all maximizers equal the transitive multipartite construction family.
technical_disposition: Digraph convention about opposite arcs and the full construction family are not supplied. Transitive constructions give lower bounds; no upper bound plus equality classification for arbitrary k.

title: Conway–Sloane's tropical theta invariant conjecture
statement_utf8:
Let $S^n_{>0}$ be the cone of positive definite quadratic forms, let $\operatorname{Parity}_n$ denote the parity characteristics, and for $A\in S^n_{>0}$ define the tropical theta constants by

$$
\Theta_v(A)=-\operatorname{cvp}(A,v).
$$

Define

$$
\Theta:S^n_{>0}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2^n-1},\qquad \Theta(A)=\left(\Theta_v(A)\right)_{v\in\operatorname{Parity}_n}.
$$

**Conway–Sloane's conjecture.** The map $\Theta$ is injective on any fundamental domain of the $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$-action on $S^n_{>0}$.

This is the tropical formulation of the assertion that the associated vonorms determine a positive definite form up to $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$-equivalence. The source states that the result is known for $n\leq4$ and conjectures it for arbitrary $n$; it also proves the claim on the matroidal locus.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every n; tropical theta map is injective on any GL_n(Z) fundamental domain of positive forms.
technical_disposition: Parity representatives and cvp normalization are unnamed. Closest-vector values on finitely many parity classes require exact arithmetic and a non-equivalence proof; no bounded candidate pair is justified.

title: The generic bigraded Hilbert-series conjecture for ideals in a product of projective lines
statement_utf8:
Let $S=k[x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1]$ with its standard bigrading, and let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subset S$, where the $f_i$ are generic bihomogeneous forms of degree $(d_i,e_i)$. For a formal power series $\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}u^iv^j$, define $[\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}u^iv^j]_+=\sum_{i,j}b_{ij}u^iv^j$, where $b_{ij}=a_{ij}$ if $a_{kl}>0$ for every $(k,l)\le(i,j)$ coordinatewise, and $b_{ij}=0$ otherwise. **The generic bigraded Hilbert-series conjecture.** The Hilbert series of $S/I$ is

$$
(S/I)(u,v)=\left[\frac{\prod_{i=1}^r(1-u^{d_i}v^{e_i})}{(1-u)^2(1-v)^2}\right]_+.
$$
 This conjecture gives the expected smallest Hilbert series for generic ideals in the coordinate ring of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$. The preceding theorem supplies a coefficientwise lower bound, and the source says the conjecture is proved for some fixed degree sequences but does not identify a general resolution.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every generic bihomogeneous degree list in k[x0,x1,y0,y1]; the Hilbert series equals the coefficientwise positive truncation of the displayed product.
technical_disposition: Base-field characteristic and allowed zero degrees need source confirmation before a counterexample. A finite Macaulay rank test would settle one degree list only; the multigraded syzygy obstruction is unbounded.

title: Kelly–Kühn–Osthus conjecture on directed cycle semidegree thresholds
statement_utf8:
An **oriented graph** is a directed graph without loops or multiple edges. For an oriented graph $G$, let $\delta^\pm(G)$ be its minimum semidegree, the smaller of its minimum indegree and minimum outdegree. For an integer $\ell\ge4$, let $k$ be the smallest integer greater than $2$ that does not divide $\ell$. **Kelly–Kühn–Osthus conjecture.** For every $\ell\ge4$ there exists $n_0:=n_0(\ell)$ such that every oriented graph $G$ on $n\ge n_0$ vertices with

$$
\delta^\pm(G) \ge \frac{n}{k}+\frac{1}{k}
$$

contains a directed cycle of length exactly $\ell$. The conjectured threshold is best possible up to the stated additive term, as shown by balanced blow-ups of a directed $k$-cycle. The conjecture is proved when $k=3$; the paper resolves the remaining cases for cycles of length divisible by $3$ but not equal to $3$.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every ell>=4; with k the smallest nondivisor>2, all sufficiently large oriented graphs of semidegree>=(n+1)/k contain an ell-cycle.
technical_disposition: The record itself reports k=3 proved and remaining multiples of3 settled. These two regimes appear exhaustive; treat as source-reported resolution requiring body restoration, not a new target. Oriented convention also must exclude antiparallel arcs.

title: Conjectured universally tight lower bound for personalized federated bandits
statement_utf8:
Let $M$ clients play a multi-armed bandit for $T$ time slots. For client $m$, let $k'_{*,m}$ denote its optimal arm, let $X'_{k,m}$ denote the reward distribution of arm $k$ for client $m$, and let $T_{k,m}$ be the expected number of pulls of arm $k$ by client $m$. Write $[M]=\{1,\ldots,M\}$, and define

$$
\beta=\alpha+\frac{1-\alpha}{M},\qquad \gamma=\frac{1-\alpha}{M},\qquad \eta=\left(\beta^2+(M-1)\gamma^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
$$

For distributions $P,Q$, let $\mathrm{kl}(P,Q)$ denote their Kullback–Leibler divergence. **Conjectured lower-bound constraint.** For any consistent algorithm $\Pi$, as $T\to\infty$, for every $m\in[M]$ and every arm $k\neq k'_{*,m}$,

$$
\frac{\beta^2}{T_{k,m}}+\sum_{n: n\neq m,\, k'_{*,n}\neq k}\frac{\gamma^2}{T_{k,n}}\leq \frac{\eta^2\mathrm{kl}(X'_{k,m},X'_{k'_{*,m},m})}{\log(T)}.
$$

This conjecture is proposed as the missing universally tight lower-bound characterization for all values of $\alpha$ in personalized federated multi-armed bandits. The preceding lower-bound results establish related constraints but do not determine the precise dependence on $\alpha$; characterizing that dependence remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every consistent algorithm, every client and nonoptimal arm, asymptotically in T; the reciprocal pull-count inequality holds for every alpha.
technical_disposition: Reward family, consistency notion and asymptotic slack are unspecified. Information lower bounds involve alternative joint instances; substituting a single KL does not justify universal tightness.

title: The conjecture on extremal normalized distance-Laplacian spectral radius
statement_utf8:
For integers $n_1,n_3\geq 1$ and $n_2\geq 2$, let $KPK_{n_1,n_2,n_3}$ be formed by taking the vertex sum of a vertex in $K_{n_1}$ with one end of $P_{n_2}$ and the vertex sum of a vertex in $K_{n_3}$ with the other end; it has $n_1+n_2+n_3-2$ vertices. For a connected graph $G$, let $\mathcal D^{\mathcal L}(G)$ be its normalized distance Laplacian matrix and let $\rho$ denote spectral radius. **Extremal normalized distance-Laplacian conjecture.** The maximum $\mathcal D^{\mathcal L}$ spectral radius among graphs on $n$ vertices tends to $2$ as $n\to\infty$ and is achieved by $KPK_{n_1,n_2,n_3}$ for some $n_1+n_2+n_3=n+2$.

The conjecture addresses the unresolved extremal graph for the normalized distance-Laplacian spectral radius; computations in the survey show that graphs of this form are extremal for $n\leq 10$.
quantifiers_reviewed: All n; a clique-path-clique maximizes normalized distance-Laplacian spectral radius, and these maxima approach2.
technical_disposition: Matrix normalization is only named; a limiting Rayleigh construction would not prove the finite-n extremizer clause. Need exact comparison against all connected graphs, not a floating eigenvalue sweep.

title: Binomial random-subset independence-gap conjecture
statement_utf8:
For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $\alpha^{**}(G)$ be the expected normalized size of a largest independent set contained in a uniformly binomial random subset of vertices, and define

$$
\epsilon^{**}(\alpha)=\inf_{G:\,\bar{\alpha}(G)\geq\alpha}\left\{\bar{\alpha}(G)-\alpha^{**}(G)\right\}.
$$

**Binomial random-subset independence-gap conjecture.** $\epsilon^{**}(\alpha)>0$ for all $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$. Equivalently, there is a monotone non-decreasing function $\epsilon^{**}:(0,1/2)\to(0,1/2)$ such that, whenever $G$ has a maximum independent set of size $\alpha n$, a binomial random subset $W$ satisfies

$$
\mathbb{E}_W[|I_W|/n]\leq\alpha-\epsilon^{**}(\alpha),
$$

where $I_W$ is the maximal independent set contained in $W$. The paper notes that this remains open even in this restricted binomial setting and records an upper bound suggested by random graphs.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every alpha in(0,1/2); a uniform positive binomial random-subset independence gap exists for all finite graphs of independence ratio>=alpha.
technical_disposition: Binomial parameter and bar-alpha normalization are not given; maximal versus maximum is inconsistent. Deletion of one fixed independent set does not control the adaptive largest independent set.

title: Klurman–Pohoata conjecture on large additive or multiplicative Sidon subsets
statement_utf8:
Let $A\boldsymbol{\subset}\mathbb R$ be finite. Define $s_+(A)$ as the size of the largest additive Sidon subset of $A$, and $s_*(A)$ as the size of the largest multiplicative Sidon subset of $A$. A set is additive Sidon if the only solutions of $a+b=c+d$ with $a,b,c,d$ in the set are the trivial ones, and multiplicative Sidon if the analogous condition holds for $ab=cd$.

**Klurman–Pohoata conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that, for every finite $A\subset\mathbb R$,

$$
\max\{s_+(A),s_*(A)\}\gg |A|^{1/2+c}.
$$

The conjecture asks whether every finite real set contains a substantially larger-than-square-root additive or multiplicative Sidon subset. The source attributes it to Klurman and Pohoata and also records their stronger conjecture with exponent $1-\epsilon$ for every $\epsilon>0$; no resolution is supplied here.
quantifiers_reviewed: There exists c>0 such that every finite real set has an additive or multiplicative Sidon subset of size >>|A|^(1/2+c).
technical_disposition: Random thinning yields the familiar square-root scale; exceeding it requires an energy dichotomy uniform over all sets. Small finite sets cannot refute unspecified c and constants.

title: Dyer–Hohlweg bijection conjecture for low elements and small inversion sets
statement_utf8:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with root system $cPhi$, positive roots $cPhi^+$, and inversion set $N(w)$ for $w
eqthinspacecin W$. A positive root $a
eqthinspacecincPhi^+$ is **small** if, for every $b
eqthinspacecincPhi^+\setminus\{a\}$, there exists $w
eqthinspacecin W$ such that $a
eqthinspacecin N(w)$ and $b
otin N(w)$. Let $cSigma$ be the set of small roots, let $cSigma(w)=cSigma\cap N(w)$, and let $cLambda$ be the set of all small inversion sets. An element $w
eqthinspacecin W$ is **low** if

$$
N(w)=coperatorname{cone}(cSigma(w))\capcPhi^+.
$$

Let $L$ be the set of low elements. **Dyer–Hohlweg's conjecture.** The map

$$
w\longmapsto cSigma(w):L\longrightarrowcLambda
$$

is a bijection between low elements and small inversion sets. This conjecture asks whether every small inversion set is realized by exactly one low element. The map is already known to be injective because inversion sets determine elements of the Coxeter group; the conjecture concerns surjectivity and its connection with the geometry of Shi regions.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every Coxeter system; the small-inversion-set map from low elements is bijective.
technical_disposition: Corrupted root notation is recoverable but the cone and realization convention need primary definitions. Injectivity is already immediate; surjectivity requires a global root-geometric construction.

title: Refined Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture for zeta maxima in macroscopic intervals
statement_utf8:
Fix $\theta>0$, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $C_k$ be the moment constants from the moment conjecture. Define

$$
\beta=\beta(\theta)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1+\theta}}.
$$

Let $\mathcal G_\theta$ be a Gumbel random variable with distribution function

$$
\mathbf{P}(\mathcal G_\theta\leq x)=\exp\left(-e^{-(x-m)/\beta}\right),
$$

where

$$
m=m(\theta)=(0.06537\dots)+\beta^2\log C_{\sqrt{1+\theta}}-\frac{\beta^2}{2}\big(\log(1+\theta)-\log(4\pi)\big).
$$

**Refined Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture.** As a sequence of random variables, the maximum satisfies

$$
\max_{|h|\leq\pi(\log T)^\theta}\log|\zeta(1/2+{\rm i}(\tau+h))|=\sqrt{1+\theta}\log\log T-\frac{1}{4\sqrt{1+\theta}}\log\log\log T+\mathcal G_{\theta,T},
$$

where $(\mathcal G_{\theta,T},T\geq1)$ converges in distribution to $\mathcal G_\theta$. This refines the conjectural law for maxima of the zeta function on macroscopic intervals by incorporating the moment correction $C_k$ into the order-one centering term. The claim is supported by theoretical and numerical evidence in the paper, but remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every theta>0; centered zeta maxima on logarithmically growing intervals converge to the specified Gumbel law.
technical_disposition: Moment constants and exact order-one centering constant are only named/numerical. Limit distribution is far beyond a finite numerical check; no full-scope route identified.

title: Hitting-time conjecture for the Erdős–Ko–Rado property in random Kneser graphs
statement_utf8:
For integers $n$ and $k$, let $K_i(n,k)$ denote the random subgraph process of the Kneser graph, and define

$$
\tau_{\alpha}=\min\left\{i:\alpha(K_i(n,k))=\binom{n-1}{k-1}\right\},
$$

$$
\tau_{\textnormal{super}}=\min\{i:K_i(n,k)\text{ has no independent superstars}\},
$$

$$
\tau_{\textnormal{near}}=\min\{i:K_i(n,k)\text{ has no independent near-stars}\},
$$

$$
\tau_{\textnormal{EKR}}=\min\{i:K_i(n,k)\text{ is EKR}\}.
$$

Here an EKR graph is one whose maximum independent sets are precisely the stars, and a near-star is a family obtained from a star by deleting one member and adding one set outside the star. **Hitting-time conjecture.** With high probability, for all $n>2k+1$,

$$
\tau_\alpha=\tau_{\textnormal{super}}\quad\text{and}\quad\tau_{\textnormal{near}}=\tau_{\textnormal{EKR}}.
$$

The corresponding equalities are proved in the paper when $n=2k+1$; the conjecture asserts that the hitting-time phenomenon extends to all larger values of $n$ and $k$.
quantifiers_reviewed: For all n>2k+1, with high probability two pairs of random Kneser hitting times coincide.
technical_disposition: The growth regime of k,n and superstar definition are missing. Proving one random threshold does not imply equality of stopping times for the entire process.

title: Wilkie's conjecture on rational points in the exponential real field
statement_utf8:
Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be definable in the o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$, and let $X^{\mathrm{alg}}$ be the union of all semi-algebraic curves contained in $X$. Define

$$
X^{\mathrm{trans}}=X\setminus X^{\mathrm{alg}}.
$$

For $q=a/b\in\mathbb{Q}$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$, let $H(q)=\max(|a|,|b|)$, extend $H$ to tuples by taking the maximum of the coordinate heights, and set

$$
X(\mathbb{Q},H)=\{x\in X\cap\mathbb{Q}^n\mid H(x)\leq H\}.
$$

**Wilkie's conjecture.** There exist constants $c=c(X)$ and $d=d(X)$ such that, for every $H\in\mathbb{N}$ with $H>e$,

$$
\left|X^{\mathrm{trans}}(\mathbb{Q},H)\right|\leq c\log(H)^d.
$$

This conjecture predicts a polylogarithmic refinement of the Pila--Wilkie counting bound for sets definable in $\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$, replacing the general bound $cH^\epsilon$. It is presented as conjectural in the source, and no resolution is supplied here.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every R_exp-definable X; exist c(X),d(X) bounding transcendental rational points of height<=H by c(log H)^d for all H>e.
technical_disposition: The Pila-Wilkie H^epsilon bound cannot yield a fixed logarithmic exponent by optimizing epsilon without uniform constants. No finite-dimensional certificate can prove all definable families.

title: Smallest singular value bound for general deterministic shifts of real Ginibre matrices
statement_utf8:
Let $X$ be an $N\times N$ real Ginibre matrix, let $A$ be a deterministic matrix, let $\gamma>0$, and define the Hermitian imaginary part by

$$
\Im A:=\frac{1}{2\mathrm{i}}(A-A^*).
$$

Write $\sigma_1(\gamma X+A)$ for the smallest singular value and let $\operatorname{Tr}(\Im A)^2$ denote the trace of $(\Im A)^2$. **General shifted real Ginibre smallest singular value conjecture.** There exist constants $c_*,C_*>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{\mathbf{P}}\left(\sigma_1(\gamma X+A)\le \frac{\sqrt{x}}{N}\right)\le C_*\frac{x}{\gamma^2}+C_*e^{-c_*\operatorname{Tr}(\Im A)^2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\gamma}\wedge\frac{x}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(\Im A)^2}\gamma^2}\right).
$$

The conjecture extends the shifted case $A=-zI$ to arbitrary deterministic matrices; the source notes that its preceding theorem proves the special case up to a logarithmic correction. The source does not state a resolution beyond this partial result.
quantifiers_reviewed: All deterministic shifts A,dimensions N and gamma>0; uniform constants give the stated smallest-singular-value tail for all x.
technical_disposition: Real Ginibre variance convention and admissible A are essential missing data. Trace(Im A)^2 alone can be unrelated to entrywise imaginary part for nonnormal real shifts; possible interpretation defect must be restored before a counterexample.

title: The extremal digraph blow-up conjecture for walks with common endpoints
statement_utf8:
Let $k$ and $t$ be positive integers. Let $\mathscr{F}_{k,t+1}$ be the family of digraphs consisting of $t+1$ different walks of length $k$ with the same initial vertex and the same terminal vertex. Let $ex(n,\mathscr{F}_{k,t+1})$ be the maximum size of an $\mathscr{F}_{k,t+1}$-free digraph of order $n$, and let $EX(n,\mathscr{F}_{k,t+1})$ be the set of such extremal digraphs. Define $z(t)$ to be the smallest integer such that, whenever $k\ge n-1\ge z(t)$, membership in $EX(n,\mathscr{F}_{k,t+1})$ is equivalent to being a transitive tournament. A balanced blow-up of the transitive tournament of order $k$ is obtained by replacing each of its $k$ vertices with independent classes whose sizes differ by at most one, and replacing every directed edge by all edges from the earlier class to the later class.

**Extremal digraph blow-up conjecture.** Let $k\ge z(t)$ and let $n$ be sufficiently large. Then $D\in EX(n,\mathscr{F}_{k,t+1})$ if and only if $D$ is a balanced blow-up of the transitive tournament of order $k$.

The conjecture seeks the extremal digraphs for forbidding $t+1$ distinct walks of length $k$ with common endpoints. It extends the known result for $k\ge 6t+1$ and sufficiently large $n$, while the asserted characterization for all $k\ge z(t)$ remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every t,k>=z(t) and sufficiently large n; all extremizers avoiding t+1 common-endpoint k-walks are balanced transitive k-blowups.
technical_disposition: A blowup certifies a lower bound only. Need show every dense alternative forces many common-endpoint walks and classify equality uniformly down to z(t); source's k>=6t+1 range is not full scope.

title: Effective maximum-principle conjecture for eigenfunctions
statement_utf8:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, nonnegative Ricci curvature, bounded second fundamental form of the boundary, and diameter $1$. Let $f$ be a function on $M$ satisfying

$$
\Delta f=\lambda f.
$$

Suppose that for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
\|f\|_{L^\infty(\partial M)}\leq\varepsilon,
$$

and that $D\subset M$ has large measure and satisfies

$$
\|\nabla f\|_{L^\infty(D)}\leq\varepsilon.
$$

**Effective maximum-principle conjecture.** Then

$$
\|f\|_{L^\infty(M)}\leq \frac{\Psi(\varepsilon\mid n,\lambda)}{\Psi_1(\operatorname{meas}(D)\mid n,\lambda)}.
$$

Here $\Psi$ and $\Psi_1$ are the functions introduced in the source. This conjecture seeks a quantitative form of the maximum principle: small boundary values and small gradient on a sufficiently large subset should force a uniformly small eigenfunction. It is used to explain the remaining difficulty in proving the corresponding essential-spectrum result.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every normalized compact manifold satisfying stated curvature/boundary controls and eigenfunction with small boundary and gradient-on-D; quantitative sup bound follows.
technical_disposition: Psi,Psi1 and large-measure threshold are undefined. Effective unique continuation may depend on geometry beyond listed controls; no precise inequality to certify.

title: Pokrovskiy's strong tournament linking conjecture
statement_utf8:
A tournament is **$r$-strong** if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves a strongly connected tournament, and its minimum in-degree and minimum out-degree are the least in-degree and out-degree among its vertices. A tournament is **$k$-linked** if, for every choice of distinct vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_k,y_1,\ldots,y_k$, there are pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths from $x_i$ to $y_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,k$. **Pokrovskiy's conjecture.** For every natural number $k$ there exists an integer $d(k)$ such that every $2k$-strong tournament with minimum in-degree and minimum out-degree at least $d(k)$ is $k$-linked.

This conjecture proposes that sufficiently large minimum in-degree and out-degree, together with $2k$-strong connectivity, force $k$-linkedness in tournaments. The source presents it as a conjecture of Pokrovskiy; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every k; exists d(k) such that all 2k-strong tournaments with min in/out degree>=d(k) are k-linked.
technical_disposition: Greedy linkage consumes connectivity and can trap the last pair. The stronger-connectivity theorem named by the source does not bridge exactly2k; no bounded constructive linkage mechanism.

title: Extension of the equivalence lemma for quasi-Hermitian varieties to odd dimensions
statement_utf8: Let $r$ be an odd integer with $r\geq 3$, and let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the coefficients appearing in the construction of the quasi-Hermitian varieties. The relevant equivalence classes are represented by matrices with the block structure described for the case treated by Lemma~. **Extension conjecture.** Lemma~ should hold for all odd $r\geq 3$: the conditions on the coefficients $\alpha$ and $\beta$ remain the same, and the block structure of the matrices representing the classes is analogous to that in Lemma~. For even $r$, the algebraic conditions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$ required to construct quasi-Hermitian varieties are different. This conjecture proposes that the odd-dimensional case has the same equivalence behavior as the established case, while the even-dimensional case requires separate algebraic conditions.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every odd r>=3 and allowed alpha,beta; an unspecified equivalence lemma and analogous block representation hold.
technical_disposition: Lemma number, coefficient hypotheses and blocks are omitted. This is not a complete mathematical statement despite the metadata flag.

title: The codegree-squared extremal conjecture for the Fano plane
statement_utf8:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be the Fano plane, and let $B_n$ be the complete balanced bipartite $3$-graph on $n$ vertices. For a $3$-graph $H$, write $\operatorname{co}_2(H)$ for its codegree squared sum and $\operatorname{exco}_2(n,\mathbb{F})$ for the maximum of $\operatorname{co}_2(H)$ over $\mathbb{F}$-free $3$-graphs $H$ on $n$ vertices. **The codegree-squared extremal conjecture for the Fano plane.** There exists $n_0$ such that for all $n\geq n_0$,

$$
\operatorname{exco}_2(n,\mathbb{F})=\operatorname{co}_2(B_n).
$$

Furthermore, $B_n$ is the unique $\mathbb{F}$-free $3$-graph $H$ on $n$ vertices satisfying $\operatorname{co}_2(H)=\operatorname{exco}_2(n,\mathbb{F})$. This is the analogue, for codegree squared density, of the solved extremal result for the Fano plane in the ordinary edge-count setting; the asserted exact extremal and uniqueness statement remains open in the supplied text.
quantifiers_reviewed: Exists n0 such that every n>=n0 Fano-free3-graph has codegree-square sum<=that of balanced bipartite3-graph, with equality only there up to isomorphism.
technical_disposition: Ordinary edge extremality does not control squared codegrees. Need a stability-plus-exactification theorem for the nonlinear objective; small n computations cannot settle an unknown n0.

title: Extremal beta-polytope intrinsic-volume limit law conjecture
statement_utf8:
Let $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with beta density

$$
p_{d,\beta}(x)=c_{d,\beta}(1-\\|x\\|^2)^\beta\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb B^d}(x),
$$

where $\beta>-1$, $\mathbb B^d=\\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\\|x\\|\leq 1\\}$, and $v_m$ denotes the $m$-th intrinsic volume. **Extremal beta-polytope conjecture.** For any fixed $d,n\in\mathbb N$, $\beta>-1$, and $m\in\\{0,1,\ldots,d\\}$, there exist positive numbers $A=A(d,m,n,\beta)$, $B=B(d,m,n,\beta)$, and $C=C(d,m,n,\beta)$ such that, for every $t$,

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[N^A\left(\max_{x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb B^d}v_m([x_1,\ldots,x_n])-\max_{1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_n\leq N}v_m([U_{i_1},\ldots,U_{i_n}])\right)\leq t\right]=1-e^{-Bt^C}.
$$

This conjectures a Weibull-type limit law, with suitable positive scaling and distribution parameters, for the deficit between the optimal intrinsic volume among all $n$-vertex polytopes in the unit ball and the largest intrinsic volume among the random beta polytopes generated by $N$ sampled points.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every d,n>=1,beta>-1,0<=m<=d; positive A,B,C give the stated Weibull deficit law for every t.
technical_disposition: m=0 or n<=m yields deterministic degenerate intrinsic volumes and defeats a nondegenerate Weibull law. This is a parameter/domain correction, no credit. Restricting to the intended nondegenerate positive-t regime leaves a hard stochastic limit.

title: The bounded-degree induced-wall conjecture
statement_utf8:
Let $W_{k\times k}$ denote the $k\times k$ wall, let a **subdivision** of a graph be obtained by replacing edges with internally vertex-disjoint paths, and let the **line graph** of a graph have one vertex for each edge, with adjacency corresponding to incident edges. For a graph $G$, write $\Delta(G)$ for its maximum degree and $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ for its treewidth.

**Bounded-degree induced-wall conjecture.** For all $k,\Delta>0$, there exists a constant $c=c(k,\Delta)$ such that every graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and treewidth more than $c$ contains, as an induced subgraph, either a subdivision of $W_{k\times k}$ or the line graph of a subdivision of $W_{k\times k}$.

This is presented as an open conjecture, with special cases proved in earlier papers of the series. The source writes $c=c(k,\delta)$ in the displayed statement, although the quantifier uses $\Delta$; the normalized statement above follows that apparent notation typo.
quantifiers_reviewed: All k,Delta>0; exists c(k,Delta) so bounded-degree graphs with treewidth>c contain an induced subdivided wall or its subdivided line graph.
technical_disposition: A grid minor alone is not induced: extra edges survive. Bounded degree does not remove all chords by an immediate pruning argument; no full induced extraction mechanism.

title: Maximum 3-separator conjecture for planar quadrangulations
statement_utf8: Let $n\geq 14$. A **3-connected planar quadrangulation** is a 3-connected planar graph in which every face is bounded by a cycle of length four. Let $\mathcal{G}^\ast$ be the class constructed by starting with a 4-cycle, successively adding vertices as described in the source construction, and gluing two disjoint copies of the cube $Q_3$ along specified 4-cycles of the resulting quadrangulation. A 3-separator is **non-trivial** when it is a 3-separator in the sense used for these quadrangulations. **Maximum 3-separator conjecture.** The $n$-vertex 3-connected planar quadrangulations with the maximum number of 3-separators are exactly the $n$-vertex graphs in $\mathcal{G}^\ast$. The construction gives graphs with exactly $4n-14$ non-trivial 3-separators, within ten of the maximum possible value by the cited lemmas; determining whether these are the unique extremal graphs remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every n>=14; extremal3-separator3-connected planar quadrangulations are exactly the source family G*.
technical_disposition: G* construction and nontrivial-separator convention are missing. The 4n-14 count is a lower construction within10 of the upper bound, not an extremal proof.

title: Conjecture on rank separations for polynomials in two variables
statement_utf8:
Let $p\in\mathbb{R}[x,y]$. The quantities $\operatorname{rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)$, $\operatorname{sep\text{-}rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)$, and $\operatorname{sos\text{-}rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)$ denote, respectively, the rank, separable rank, and sum-of-squares rank of $p$, with separable rank taken with respect to the local sum-of-squares cones. The polynomial $p$ is understood to be separable in the first two cases and a sum of squares in the third.

**Rank-separation conjecture.** There exist no functions $f,g,h\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $p\in\mathbb{R}[x,y]$, independently of the degree of $p$,

$$
\operatorname{sep\text{-}rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)\leq f\bigl(\operatorname{rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)\bigr),
$$

$$
\operatorname{sep\text{-}rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)\leq g\bigl(\operatorname{sos\text{-}rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)\bigr),
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{sos\text{-}rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)\leq h\bigl(\operatorname{rank}_{\Lambda_1}(p)\bigr).
$$

The conjecture asserts that rank measures for polynomials can exhibit unbounded separations even when the number of variables is fixed and the degree is unrestricted; the preceding constructions establish analogous separations for bounded-degree polynomials, but the two-variable, arbitrary-degree case remains posed as a conjecture.
quantifiers_reviewed: No degree-independent functions separately bound the three indicated polynomial rank comparisons in two variables.
technical_disposition: Lambda1 and the decomposition cones are undefined and no-functions wording needs separate-versus-simultaneous quantifier restoration. Encoding a tensor by high powers may destroy positivity decompositions; no faithful bridge established.

title: Configuration-count conjecture for merges of vincular patterns
statement_utf8:
Let $\sigma$ be a vincular pattern with $j$ blocks, let $k$ denote its length, and let $M_{\underline{\sigma}}$ be the relevant maximum common-block size. For $1\leq l\leq M_{\underline{\sigma}}$, let $c_{\sigma,l}$ be the number of possible configurations for a merge of two copies of $\underline{\sigma}$ in which the minimum size of the two merged blocks is $l$. Let $b'_{\sigma}(2k-l,2j-1)$ be the number of merges of two copies of $\underline{\sigma}$ with $l$ common elements and $2j-1$ blocks that correspond to one of these $c_{\sigma,l}$ configurations.

**Configuration-count conjecture.** For every vincular pattern $\sigma$ with $j$ blocks and every $1\leq l\leq M_{\underline{\sigma}}$, 

$$
b'_{\sigma}(2k-l,2j-1)>\frac{\binom{2k-l}{k}}{k_{(l)}}c_{\sigma,l}.
$$

The authors state that this conjecture would imply the relevant inequality for vincular patterns, and consequently the associated theorem and central limit theorem for vincular patterns. The conjecture is presented without a resolution in the supplied text.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every vincular pattern sigma and1<=l<=maximum block length; its restricted self-merge count exceeds the displayed random-merge expectation.
technical_disposition: Primary Conj6.7 supplies the missing max-block definition and merge interpretation; Section6 theorem concerns aggregated variance positivity, not each l. Singleton-pattern equality would be a domain endpoint correction only. No full valid-pattern counting route found.
